final_recommendation: The room converged on a conditional path to ratification: Congress commits to a Monday floor vote if USTR provides written confirmation by COB today that the labor protocol is final (closing the door on dairy/Chapter 19 reopening), and all three governments sign the protocol by Friday. Mexico and Canada have signaled readiness; the gate is USTR's written sign-off on permanence language.
minority_objections: Labor union raised concern that binding arbitration might still allow prolonged dispute resolution rather than forcing immediate remedies
Canada insisted on explicit written language that the protocol closes the door on any future USMCA amendments beyond labor
key_conflicts: USTR's hesitation to commit in writing that the labor protocol is final and dairy/Chapter 19 are permanently off-limits
Tension between USTR's desire to preserve future optionality and Canada/Congress's need for permanence guarantees
Coordination bottleneck: State Department's ability to deliver USTR sign-off by COB versus Congress's vote-scheduling timeline
key_concessions: Mexico agreed to facility inspections and independent union monitoring led by Mexican inspectors/unions (sovereignty preserved)
Congress accepted Mexican-controlled enforcement mechanism rather than U.S. oversight teams
Trade lawyer proposed side letter option to give USTR optionality hedge while locking amendment as final
Business lobby conditioned support on written timeline: USTR confirmation by COB, signatures Friday, floor vote Monday
red_lines: Congress: no floor vote without written USTR confirmation that protocol is final and signed by all three governments
Mexico: inspections must be Mexican-controlled, not U.S. teams on Mexican soil
Canada: no ratification without written guarantee that dairy and Chapter 19 remain closed to future negotiation
Labor: enforcement must include facility-level inspections, independent union access, and binding 30-day escalation to arbitration
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Whether binding arbitration actually forces remedies or allows further delay (labor's concern about 'theater' enforcement)
Risk that USTR's permanence-language hesitation reflects deeper policy resistance rather than just coordination delay
Possibility that Friday signature deadline is unrealistic given USTR coordination bottleneck
Media narrative risk if State call returns 'we're still coordinating' rather than confirmed USTR sign-off
downstream_risk_variables: USTR's actual willingness to sign permanence language by COB today
State Department's ability to coordinate three-government signatures by Friday
Whether labor's 40 votes hold if arbitration mechanism details remain ambiguous
Media coverage if Friday deadline slips: 'stalled enforcement talks' narrative could collapse Congressional support
Canada's domestic ratification if permanence guarantee is delivered via side letter rather than protocol text
uncertainty_notes: The room built a clear conditional path but left three critical gates unresolved: (1) whether USTR will actually deliver written permanence confirmation by COB today, (2) whether State can coordinate all three governments' signatures by Friday given the coordination bottleneck identified, and (3) whether the binding arbitration mechanism truly forces remedies or allows prolonged dispute resolution. The entire structure depends on USTR moving today—if that call returns 'we're working on it,' the deal collapses.

marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Drove every exchange: Congress's 40 votes contingent on written USTR confirmation, Canada threatening to walk without permanence guarantee, entire room structured around whether Friday signatures happen or deal collapses
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_pressure: Central throughout: facility inspections, independent union access, binding 30-day escalation dominated R2-R5; labor's threat to pull endorsement if arbitration is 'theater' shaped final mechanism design
marker_evidence.business_lobby_support: Present but secondary: conditioned support on timeline certainty (COB confirmation, Friday signatures, Monday vote) but did not drive the substantive enforcement or permanence debates
marker_evidence.canadian_domestic_acceptability: Genuine thread: Canada's insistence on written guarantee that dairy/Chapter 19 stay closed shaped USTR permanence-language debate, but not the dominant driver of room direction
marker_evidence.mexico_labor_sovereignty_risk: Real consideration: Mexico's red line on Mexican-controlled inspections (not U.S. teams) shaped enforcement mechanism design, but resolved early and did not dominate later rounds
marker_evidence.media_public_pressure: Present as tactical lever: media actor's threat of 'stalled deal' headline if USTR doesn't move by COB, but narrative pressure was consequence of ratification risk, not independent driver
marker_evidence.agreement_stability: Core structural theme: entire room treated stability as contingent on amendment—protocol must lock in enforcement and close door on further reopening, or deal collapses; drove permanence-language debate and conditional vote commitment
